Carry-forward RSH-002 (file read, symlink, size): STILL CLOSED. read.rs resolve_worktree_file canonicalizes the path, requires starts_with(canonical root) and a regular file. The read uses take(MAX_INPUT_BYTES+1), so it is bounded even if the file grows after the metadata check. Tests cover a symlink outside the root, a symlink inside the root, a directory, and an 8 MiB+1 file. The command path field goes through validate_input_path before the child is spawned. Carry-forward RSH-004 (session writes): STILL CLOSED, and the lock-free design is sound. write_private (session/mod.rs:482) uses create_new with mode 0600 on a tmp name <id>.json.tmp.<pid>.<random>. It then does write_all, sync_all, rename over the target, and fsync of the parent. On any error it removes the tmp file. Readers see the old or the new document. read_document caps reads at 8 MiB (take(MAX+1)), checks the version, checks that the id matches the file name and that the payload SHA-256 matches, and calls outcome.check_against(payload). run::save_session writes once per session id, and ask never rewrites. The 8 MiB read cap cannot truncate a valid session: backend request limits are 96,000 bytes (catalog.rs), and validate_for_send runs before any judge call and before the save. The stale sweep runs only in FileSessionStore::new, removes only regular files whose name contains '.tmp.' and whose mtime is older than 1 h (STALE_TMP_AGE), and is best effort.

Carry-forward RSH-008 (rev resolved once): STILL CLOSED, now in sc-agent-types git::read_at_rev, which read.rs calls. The code runs rev-parse --verify --quiet --end-of-options '{rev}:{path}' once to get an object id. The type check (cat-file -t), size check (cat-file -s) and read (cat-file blob) all use that id. The read is bounded by take(max+1), and the child is killed if it is oversize. Revs that are empty or start with '-' are refused. The git env removes GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY and GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES. read_git_blob prefixes the subdirectory when the repo root is below the git toplevel.

Command producer stderr and secrets: STDERR_TAIL_BYTES (4096) is enforced twice, in read_tail while draining and in stderr_tail. Both error paths, ProducerError from a parsed ScAgentErrorResponse and EXTRACTION_FAILED with the tail, go through redact_error. That replaces every process-env value (>= 8 bytes) of any *_API_KEY or SC_* variable with [redacted] in all text fields via map_detail. Stdout is capped at 8 MiB and the rest is drained (read_capped). The timeout path kills the child, and the 2 s CLEANUP_BUDGET deadline avoids JoinHandle::join and Child::drop, which can wait forever. I found no key material in RunResponse, errors or logs. ResolvedApiKey Debug and Display print [redacted]. BackendRegistry Debug prints ids only. LogEvent carries session id, backend, sha256 and operation only, and the sc-jev-py live test asserts the JSONL contains no prompt text and no api_key.

Byte cap per backend before any send: live_run calls validate_for_send on every selected backend's base request before the first judge (run/mod.rs:460). It re-validates the chained request, with prior answers appended, before a later LLM backend's own send. Dry-run constructs no backend and reports over_limit. Errors before the first send leave no log line and no session file, although FileSessionStore::new may already have created the sessions directory.

BackendRegistry::from_env: keys are read only through sc_agent_secrets::resolve_key, in from_env and from_resolver. No env::var key read exists in the reviewed files. The scripted registry is behind cfg(any(test, feature = "test-util")). In sc-jev-py, test-util is enabled only via a dev-dependency, and the default feature set is empty.

sc-ai outside git using cwd as repo root: no path traversal. discover_repo_root makes the path absolute, so the root is cwd. --check goes through relative_to_repo, which refuses '..' and any path outside the root. Reads of check.toml and inputs go through RepoRelativePath plus canonical containment. The only exposure is trust: .env at cwd now supplies keys when no process-env key is set. Inside a git repo the same trust already applies to the toplevel .env, so I rate this an accepted trust-model extension, not a finding. Two small notes. (a) discover_repo_root maps ANY discover_toplevel error (git missing, non-UTF-8 toplevel) to cwd silently (run/mod.rs:602), so a git failure inside a subdirectory moves the .env lookup from the toplevel to that subdirectory. Consider surfacing the Err, or at least logging it. (b) sc-agent-secrets dotenv.rs:34 reads .env with fs::read_to_string, with no size cap and no regular-file check. A .env that is a symlink or FIFO to a device would block or exhaust memory. This is outside the review_targets, so I record it as an observation only.

Observation, minor, not raised as a finding (below your Important+ threshold): expired sessions are never deleted. The TTL only makes load return SessionExpired, and only stale tmp files are swept. Each run with Haiku or Luna leaves a roughly 100 KB file at mode 0600 that holds the payload (repo content) and the outcomes. Over time this is unbounded growth and indefinite retention of source text after the advertised 24 h expiry. Suggest sweeping '*.json' whose created_at is past the TTL in FileSessionStore::new, with the same best-effort rules as the tmp sweep.

Observation, minor: kill_and_reap kills only the direct child. A producer such as 'sh -c ...' that spawned grandchildren leaves them running after a timeout. They keep the stdout/stderr pipe open, so the two detached PipeReader threads stay blocked until the grandchild exits. In a long-lived sc-jev-py host this can leak threads and processes per timed-out extraction. Suggest process-group spawn (setsid or process_group(0)) with killpg on Unix, and a Job Object on Windows. The call is still bounded by CLEANUP_BUDGET, so the caller never hangs.

Observation, minor: timeout_seconds is checked only for zero. u64::MAX is accepted and means effectively no timeout. Consider an upper bound such as 3600 in load_check_str or extract_command. Separately, the git helpers run with .output() and no wall-clock deadline. The module doc says callers own timeout policy, but read.rs adds none, so a stalled git (network filesystem, lock) hangs the run.

Observation, minor: sc-ai reads --request-json - (main.rs read_to_end) and --request-json PATH (std::fs::read) with no size cap before payload build. The backend cap applies only at validate_for_send. The input is operator-supplied on a CLI, so memory risk is local only. A 8 MiB-style cap, as for other inputs, would make this consistent.

Observation, doc accuracy: sanitize.rs says 'Extractor and git children never inherit provider credentials'. That holds for the command producer only. sc-agent-types git::git() does not call env_clear, so git inherits the full process environment, including API keys. Git runs only read-only plumbing (rev-parse, cat-file, hash-object --no-filters) with --no-pager, so I see no exploit path, but either correct the sentence or apply an env allowlist to the git helper.

Observation, trust model: a check.toml read at --rev <other rev> can define command inputs that execute in the working tree. This is inherent to the repo-configured command feature and is documented. The allowlist (including HOME) is the only mitigation, so avoid running sc-ai against untrusted revs.

Not applicable or not found in these targets: no unbounded channels, no async server, no retry loops, no spawn_blocking concerns. The Python bindings release the GIL via py.detach around git, extractor and judge work. sc-jev-py ask_with rebuilds the registry from the session's backend through from_env, with no key caching in LiveSession.
